features.description: When a loaded primary dentry names an ino that is already in cache under another dentry, CDir::_load_dentry logs clog error "loaded dup inode `<ino>` ... already exists at ..." and does not link it, so the name is absent from lookups and listings. No damage-table entry is created, so only the cluster log shows the loss. mds_hack_allow_loading_invalid_metadata (default false, test aid) links it anyway.

features.group: Damage detection, DamageTable and its effects
features.name: Fatal damage takes the rank down:damaged
features.summary: Damage to a rank's own stray structures or the root directory, or table overflow, stops the rank until an operator repairs it.
features.description: notify_dentry is fatal for dentries in the rank's own mdsdir or stray dirs; notify_dirfrag for frags of the rank's own stray dirs or of the root directory (on any rank); every notify_* when by_id.size() > mds_damage_table_max_entries, checked before the duplicate test so even a repeat report is fatal once over the limit. CDir::go_bad, CDir::go_bad_dentry (and so scrub's dentry check) and MDCache::_open_remote_dentry_finish honour the result by calling MDSRank::damaged(), which sets want-state down:damaged, flushes the cluster log, sends a beacon and waits up to mds_mon_shutdown_timeout (5 s) for the ack under mds_lock, then respawns. No daemon takes a damaged rank until an operator fixes the metadata and runs "ceph mds repaired"; its metadata is unavailable meanwhile. Scrub's backtrace results and the uninline failures ignore the fatal result, so on overflow those reports are dropped silently.
features.notes: Damage to the rank's own mdsdir dirfrag is not fatal. Other MDSRank::damaged() triggers (unloadable tables, sessionmap or journal, root open failure, ...) and the down:damaged rank state are owned by 01-cluster-membership-and-ha.

features.group: Damage detection, DamageTable and its effects
features.name: damage ls and damage rm commands
features.summary: Lets operators list a rank's damage entries and clear them after fixing the metadata.
features.description: "damage ls" (asok or tell, any rank, per-rank table) dumps a JSON array of entries with damage_type (dir_frag, dentry, backtrace, uninline), id, ino and type-specific fields: frag; frag, dname and snap_id; rank, errno (string) and scrub_tag; plus path. "damage rm `<damage_id>`" erases by id; a missing id is a silent no-op and a missing argument returns -EINVAL. Only the table entry is removed: STATE_BADFRAG and STATE_BADREMOTEINO stay on cached objects, so after rm a BADFRAG dirfrag (cached complete and normally empty) gives -ENOENT instead of -EIO until it is trimmed and refetched, and committing it would hit the dirfrag stat guard and turn the rank read-only if the object is missing.
features.notes: reported_at is recorded but not dumped. Erasing one DENTRY entry erases the whole per-dirfrag dentry map from the lookup index while the other ids stay listed. UNINLINE_FILE entries show the global errno rather than the failure errno (code reading). Damage ids are random 32-bit values; an unknown id in damage rm returns rc 0. The table is not persisted, so it is empty after a restart or failover. Documented operator procedure: `ceph tell mds.<id> damage ls|rm` (damaged-rank.rst). Command plane: F-ADM-050.

legacy_parts.note: The 'uninline' damage_type in damage ls with its rank, errno and scrub_tag fields, and the note on its errno value. Entries of this type are created only from scrub uninline failures (F-BG-052). The other damage types are current.

features.group: Damage detection, DamageTable and its effects
features.name: EIO for requests that touch known damage
features.summary: Fails client requests fast with EIO when their path crosses metadata in the damage table.
features.description: MDCache::path_traverse returns -EIO when it reaches a dirfrag in the table (before fetching it or when looking up the next component), when the next component is a dentry in the table (exact (dirfrag, name, snapid) match), and when it follows an uncached remote dentry whose target ino has BACKTRACE damage. Requests waiting on a full dirfrag fetch that turns out damaged are woken with -EIO; C_MDS_RetryRequest ignores the code, so the request retries and hits these checks. Damage entries never put the MDS into read-only mode.
features.notes: path_traverse does not fetch a dirfrag recorded as damaged. See also F-CACHE-041 (path traversal).

features.group: Damage detection, DamageTable and its effects
features.name: readdir behaviour on damaged directories
features.summary: Lists what can be listed of a damaged directory without returning an error.
features.description: handle_client_readdir and try_open_auth_dirfrag do not consult the damage table. A BADFRAG dirfrag is marked complete, so readdir succeeds and lists only the dentries that happened to be cached already (normally none). A dentry whose value failed to decode is simply absent, and a remote dentry with STATE_BADREMOTEINO is skipped. readdir never returns EIO for damage.
features.notes: Established by code reading.
